claims.text: A data-driven machine-learning framework can be used to optimize thermo-mechanical processing for concurrent strength–ductility improvement in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations can overcome the strength–ductility trade-off in tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys.
Conventionally processed refractory high-entropy alloys typically exhibit high strength at the expense of ductility.
The strength–ductility trade-off in conventionally processed refractory high-entropy alloys is caused by a homogeneous microstructure.
Machine learning can analyze high-throughput experimental and simulation data to identify optimized processing parameters for these alloys.
Optimizing rolling reduction, aging temperature, and aging time can induce controlled stepwise coherent nanoprecipitations.
The relevant strength–ductility improvement can occur under ambient-temperature tensile deformation.
The engineered microstructure contains coherent nanoprecipitates and δ-lamellae coupled with γ″ particles.
Coherent precipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
The coherent precipitate architecture relieves local stress concentrations that could otherwise initiate premature cracks.
Dislocations can shear the coherent δ-lamellae while being pinned by γ″ particles.
Shearing of δ-lamellae provides plastic accommodation rather than producing cracks.
Balancing dislocation barriers with plastic accommodation enables simultaneous strength and ductility improvement.
A tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy with SCCPs can exhibit a strength above 2 GPa and tensile ductility above 10% at ambient temperature.
Machine-learning-optimized processing will produce strength around or above 2 GPa and tensile ductility above 10%.
Machine-learning-optimized samples will outperform conventionally processed samples concurrently in strength and ductility.
Applicability of the proposed approach to other alloy systems or non-ambient conditions remains unverified.
The optimal machine-learning-derived processing parameters and exact quantitative property improvements require experimental validation.
